memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of gout, chronic urticaria and anxiety.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports occasional toe pain, intermittent itchy wheals and mild worry about work.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.0 (obese). No active joint swelling, skin shows scattered papules, no distress.
IMPRESSION: 1) Gout – serum uric acid elevated. 2) Chronic urticaria – stable. 3) Generalised anxiety disorder – on escitalopram and buspirone, GAD‑7 score 6 (mild).
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue allopurinol 100 mg OD, levocetirizine 5 mg OD, escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD. Advise weight reduction, low‑purine diet, regular exercise. Offer influenza vaccine in autumn. Return if severe joint pain, worsening rash, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C or suicidal thoughts.

Reason for visit: review of gout control and urticaria.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes mild ankle discomfort after long drives, occasional itchy patches, anxiety unchanged.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). No joint effusion, skin shows faint wheals.
IMPRESSION: Gout – uric acid still high; consider increasing allopurinol. Urticaria – stable. Anxiety – GAD‑7 5.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase allopurinol to 200 mg OD. Continue levocetirizine, escitalopram, buspirone. Advise diet, weight loss, hydration. Offer influenza vaccine in autumn. Return if severe joint pain, fever, rash worsening, shortness of breath.

Reason for visit: Influenza vaccination and chronic disease review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no new joint pain, mild itchy lesions on arms, anxiety stable.
EXAMINATION: BP 129/81 mmHg, weight 76 kg, BMI 26.3 (overweight). No acute inflammation, skin shows few papules.
IMPRESSION: Gout – uric acid trending down. Urticaria – mild. Anxiety – GAD‑7 4.
ARRANGEMENTS: Administered inactivated influenza vaccine (0.5 mL IM) today. Continue allopurinol 200 mg OD, levocetirizine, escitalopram, buspirone. Advise continue diet, exercise. Return if high fever, severe rash, joint swelling, breathing difficulty, or suicidal ideation.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: gout flare after long haul.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports severe pain in left big toe for 2 days, swelling, difficulty walking. Urticaria mild, anxiety unchanged.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/86 mmHg, weight 79 kg, BMI 27.3 (obese). Left first MTP joint swollen, tender, warm. Skin shows scattered wheals.
IMPRESSION: Acute gout flare – uric acid risen. Urticaria stable. Anxiety – GAD‑7 6.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start colchicine 0.5 mg BD for 5 days, continue allopurinol 200 mg OD, consider increasing to 300 mg OD after flare. Continue levocetirizine, escitalopram, buspirone. Advise rest, ice, hydration, low‑purine diet. Offer influenza vaccine next autumn. Return if fever >38.5°C, worsening joint pain, chest pain, breathlessness, or suicidal thoughts.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review after gout flare and medication tolerance.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports toe pain resolved, no new lesions, anxiety mild.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). No joint swelling, skin clear.
IMPRESSION: Gout – uric acid still elevated despite allopurinol; consider switching to febuxostat. Urticaria – controlled. Anxiety – GAD‑7 5.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop allopurinol. Start febuxostat 40 mg OD. Continue levocetirizine, escitalopram, buspirone. Advise weight management, avoid alcohol, stay hydrated. Offer influenza vaccine in coming autumn. Return if severe joint pain, rash, fever >39°C, chest pain, breathlessness, or suicidal thoughts.
